title: Epochal Driver Impact Study: Cloud SKUs (A100 / H100 / L40S)
summary: Controlled comparison of performance between common cloud GPU SKUs (A100 variants, H100, L40S) across multiple NVIDIA driver / CUDA combinations. Goal: surface regressions and identify stable driver+kernel pairings for production serving and Dedicated fleet provisioning.
motivation: We observed intermittent tail-latency regressions in December that correlated with provider-side driver updates. This study tries to (1) quantify end-to-end p50/p95/p99 behavior across drivers, (2) identify microkernel hotspots that change between driver versions, and (3) produce concrete rollout rules to avoid regressions during cloud SKU upgrades.
test_matrix:
SKUs tested:
- A100: 40GB (cloud-standard-a100-40)
- A100: 80GB (cloud-pro-a100-80)
- H100: 80GB (cloud-h100-80)
- L40S: 48GB (cloud-l40s-48)
Driver/CUDA combos:
- NVIDIA driver 535.104 + CUDA 11.8
- NVIDIA driver 545.89 + CUDA 12.1
- NVIDIA driver 555.30 + CUDA 12.2
- Provider-vendored optimized kernel stack (when available)
Workloads:
- Small-chat (prompt 64 tokens, response 128 tokens)
- Long-context generation (prompt 4k tokens -> generate 2k tokens)
- KV-cache heavy retrieval (repeated prefix queries)
- Batch packing 16x small requests
- Persistent streaming (continuous token stream for 5 minutes)
Note: each combination run for 60 minutes steady-state after a 10-minute warmup.
methodology:
1) Bring up single-instance test VMs in each cloud region with pinned instance types to avoid noisy neighbors.
2) Deploy identical container images (runtime pinned to branch/inference-v2.3) containing our runtime binary with tracing enabled.
3) Run microbenchmarks (kernel timings, cudaMemcpy, pci-e transfers) and end-to-end harness (grpc client driving model via Redis-backed queue) simultaneously.
4) Capture perf traces (Nsight CPU+GPU sampling), CUDA profiler summaries, NVML power/temperature, and our runtime-level metrics (queue depth, batch sizes, token-per-second).
5) Repeat each run 3x across different times of day; median used for comparative tables, full traces archived.
6) For anomalous cases, re-run with verbose driver debug logs and reduced NPUs to reproduce.
hardware_config:
Nodes used (single-GPU tests):
- a100-40: 1x A100-40GB, 64 vCPU, 512GB RAM, PCIe
- a100-80: 1x A100-80GB, 64 vCPU, 768GB RAM, NVLink disabled
- h100-80: 1x H100-80GB, 96 vCPU, 1TB RAM, NVLink enabled
- l40s-48: 1x L40S-48GB, 64 vCPU, 384GB RAM, PCIe
Interconnect notes: where possible, NVLink was toggled to match provider defaults. Local SSD used for model load, network I/O disabled for generation workload.
software_config:
Base OS: Ubuntu 22.04 minimal image with AMI/kernel patches from provider.
Runtime build: serving-runtime v2.3.1 (commit: a1b2c3d) with profiling hooks and token-level timing.
CUDA / Driver matrix: as listed in test_matrix. cuDNN versions matched to CUDA (cuDNN 8.x). Container runtime: containerd 1.6.6.
Note: we purposely avoided using provider-side optimized images (except one test) to isolate driver effects.
workloads:
- Small-chat (S): 1 prompt + generate 128 tokens, concurrency 32
- Long-gen (L): 4k token prompt, generate 2k tokens, concurrency 2
- KV-iterate (K): repeated prefix queries reusing KV-cache with variable context resize, concurrency 16
- Batch-pack (B): pack up to 16 short prompts into single batch
- Stream-long (T): continuous streaming generation for 5 minutes per connection
Each workload annotated in traces; sampling at 1s per-metric resolution and full token traces for 1% of requests.
measurement_metrics:
- E2E p50/p95/p99 latency (ms)
- Tokens/sec (aggregate per GPU)
- Kernel time breakdown (matmul, softmax, layernorm, embedding lookup)
- PCIe / NVLink transfer time (ms per transfer)
- CUDA context switch overhead (ms)
- Power (W) and thermal throttling events
- Memory fragmentation / OOM incidents
results_summary:
High-level findings (median across runs):
- H100 + driver 545.89 showed best absolute tokens/sec on Long-gen (+18% vs A100-80 with 545.89), but tail p99 for streaming spiked on 555.30 builds.
- A100-80 with driver 535.104 had consistently stable p95/p99 across workloads but ~6% lower throughput than with 545.89 where matmul kernels were faster.
- L40S delivered competitive small-chat latency but had a larger per-token variance under KV-cache churn (p99 amplification ~2.2x).
- Kernel-level diffs: newer drivers moved certain matmul workloads from cuBLASGemmEx->cutlass path, reducing matmul latency on H100 but increasing small-matrix launch overhead on A100 (observed in small-batch chat).
- PCIe transfer stalls: particular on a100-40 with driver 555.30 we saw periodic 10–40ms DMA stalls correlated with host kernel preemption events (reproducible).
- Memory residency: CUDA 12.2 stacks improved async memcpy overlap on H100 but exposed a bug in our allocator that increased fragmentation on L40S images.
observations:
1) Not all driver upgrades are net-positive: driver 555.30 improved throughput for large-matrix workloads but introduced tail spikes for small-request streaming on A100 families.
2) Provider-specific kernel bundles (when present) sometimes outperform generic driver+CUDA pairs but are brittle across kernel versions — makes long-term fleet stability risky.
3) NVLink on H100 reduced host->device transfer variance substantially for long-context workloads; recommend enabling where available for Dedicated pools.
4) Our runtime’s batch packing interacts sensitively with matmul kernel selection: when kernel path changes to cutlass, small-batch overhead increases and batching yields diminish.
5) Traces indicate kernel launch serialization as a dominant contributor to tail on A100 for small-chat when driver switches to cutlass path.
anomalies:
- Reproducible DMA stalls on A100-40 with driver 555.30: host-side preemption + driver GC combined to cause 10–40ms stalls every ~60s under steady streaming. Hypothesis: new DMA scheduling in driver interacts poorly with our pinned memory allocator.
- H100 with driver 535.104 had an odd kernel fallback for attention softmax (higher register usage) producing +12% latency on long-gen; resolved in later driver.
- L40S fragmentation: CUDA 12.2 async memcpy path reduced overlap for chunked KV-cache writes leading to transient OOM in high-concurrency runs (seen twice across all tests).
action_items: Pin default production fleets to driver 545.89 + CUDA 12.1 for now (best stability/throughput tradeoff observed)
Add driver-version canary in rollout playbook: run small-chat/streaming suite for 6h before fleet-wide promotion
Implement allocator instrumentation to log pinned memory region lifetimes and DMA queue stalls
Enable NVLink in Dedicated H100 pools by default and document fallback behavior
Add automated microbenchmark to CI that detects kernel-path changes (cuBLAS->cutlass) and flags potential small-batch regressions
next_steps:
1) Re-run failing A100-40 555.30 case with reduced allocator aggressiveness and host preemption disabled to confirm root cause.
2) Create a small Dedicated pilot on 545.89/CUDA12.1 with NVLink enabled for customers with long-context usage patterns.
3) Publish a short internal note for SRE + customer-success about potential perf changes around driver bumps and recommended mitigation steps (pinning/canary).
4) Extend test harness to include provider-vendored kernel bundles and capture per-kernel binary IDs for future attribution.
